title: A common word
hookLine: come to a word common between us: to worship none but Allah (3:64)

cards: October 2007. A letter goes out from Muslim scholars and leaders, more than a hundred and thirty of them, Sunni and Shia, from many countries.
It's addressed to the Pope, to Orthodox patriarchs, to the Archbishop of Canterbury, and to the leaders of Christian churches everywhere.
Its title is a phrase lifted straight out of a verse in Al 'Imran: a common word between us and you.

teach.b: Here's 3:64 in Pickthall's words: "Say: O People of the Scripture! Come to an agreement between us and you: that we shall worship none but Allah." Pickthall says agreement.
The Arabic is kalimatin sawa', a word that is level, the same for both sides.

teach.h: AHL AL-KITAB: PEOPLE OF THE SCRIPTURE
teach.b: People of the Scripture, ahl al-kitab, is the Qur'an's name for Jews and Christians, those given scripture before, in the Qur'an's terms.
The verse goes on: that we ascribe no partner to God, and that none of us take others as lords beside God. And if they turn away, say: bear witness that we are Muslims, those who have surrendered.
Notice what the verse doesn't do. It doesn't threaten. It invites, names the ground it believes both sides share, and if the answer is no, it asks the other side to witness where Muslims stand.
Commentators such as Ibn Kathir connect this part of the surah to a delegation of Christians from Najran who came to Medina to talk with the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ.
A hadith in Sahih al-Bukhari reports that when the Prophet wrote to Heraclius, the Byzantine emperor, his letter included this very verse.
The 2007 letter built on two commandments it found in both scriptures: love of God, and love of neighbor. Christian leaders wrote back, and meetings followed.
Muslims and Christians still differ on central things, and the verse itself names some of them.
But it opens with the word common.

how: Muslims cite 3:64 in interfaith conversation; in 2007 Muslim scholars and leaders addressed an open letter titled 'A Common Word Between Us and You' to Christian leaders, built on love of God and love of neighbor.

games.q: you invite someone to a word common between you. they turn away. what does 3:64 say to do?
o: say: bear witness that we are those who have surrendered to God.
games.why: the verse simply asks them to witness where Muslims stand. no threat, no pursuit.

practice: Picture a table between you and a neighbor, coworker or relative whose beliefs aren't yours, and instead of your differences, set down the things you both care about: the people you love, honesty, a good day's work, maybe a God you each pray to in your own way.
Look at what's on the table and find one sentence you could both say and mean.
